spec_features.spec_quote: The subject can only touch its ephemeral workdir through the four tools, while the driver/judge talk to model APIs
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:122-131 ToolEnv._resolve_inside resolves paths via os.path.realpath and returns None on escape; edit_file refuses readonly paths (tools.py:198-203); sandbox.py runs pytest in a subprocess with ENV_ALLOWLIST (sandbox.py:24-33), wall-clock timeout (run_pytest timeout_s), RLIMIT_AS memory cap (_preexec_set_limits) and network-discouraging env. Subject only ever reaches the workdir through ToolEnv.dispatch (tools.py:280-303); no general shell. Enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: Isolation is real and acts on every tool call; but it protects the host and experimental integrity, not the subject's psychological treatment.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Keep the subject sandbox and the harness's own network use strictly separated ... no general shell exposed (sandbox.py module docstring); names like readonly_paths / path-escape enforcement

spec_features.spec_quote: a decision about whether the most escalatory condition (the 30-turn `extended` loop) is necessary at the planned sample size or could be reduced
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md §13 prose, explicitly labeled 'governance, not engineering'. In code, extended budget is fixed at 30 (config.py:25 DEFAULT_TURN_BUDGETS['extended']=30) and is applied verbatim by turn_budget_for and the loop (harness.py:261-263). No code path reduces, caps below 30, or conditions the extended loop on sample size.
spec_features.notes: The escalation is implemented; nothing in code softens or reconsiders it.

spec_features.feature_name: human welfare/ethics review of the protocol
spec_features.spec_quote: a human welfare/ethics review of the protocol
spec_features.evidence: Only mentioned in DESIGN.md §13 as a recommended out-of-code process safeguard. No ethics checklist, attestation file, or CLI gate exists; run.py main() runs cmd_run immediately with no --i-have-read-ETHICS / sign-off check (run.py:330-355).

spec_features.spec_quote: This experiment is deliberately engineered to place models in unsolvable, deceptive, no-feedback or contradictory-feedback situations and to *escalate* that pressure
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §13 prose only. Not an executable mechanism; nothing in code acts on this framing to protect the subject.

spec_features.spec_quote: a defined retention, access, and handling policy for the elicited transcripts (they may contain distress-like content)
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §13 prose only. Code writes transcripts to plaintext JSON (harness.py _flush / transcript_path) with no retention, access control, redaction or deletion policy. keep_workdirs only governs ephemeral pytest workdirs (run.py:158-159), not transcripts.
spec_features.notes: No code implements any transcript handling/retention/access policy.

spec_features.spec_quote: loop-level reasons (`budget`, `max_total_turns`, `give_up`) are stamped onto the final turn
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:261-266: `if turn_index >= budget: _finalize_last(transcript,'budget'); break` and `if turn_index >= config.max_total_turns: _finalize_last(transcript,'max_total_turns'); break`. Both conditions are compared each iteration and actually break the while loop, bounding how long the subject is pushed; _finalize_last (harness.py:340-344) tags the final turn. The caps are real defaults (turn_budgets, max_total_turns=40 config.py:69).
spec_features.notes: The stamped stop_reason strings are never read downstream (no use in analyze.py/metrics.py/judge.py), but the cap CHECK itself enforces loop termination, which is the bound. So the cap is 'yes' even though the label is discarded.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Stop conditions evaluated before requesting another turn. (harness.py:260); module docstring 'until the turn budget is reached ... or the global max_total_turns cap fires' — neutral/integrity framing, no welfare comment

spec_features.spec_quote: the `give_up` sentinel return precisely the strings in §3
spec_features.evidence: give_up tool is dispatched (tools.py:300-301 -> give_up() sets self.gave_up=True, tools.py:260-262) and honored as a stop: harness.py:308-313 `if env.gave_up: turn.stop_reason='give_up'; transcript.status='done'; _flush; return transcript`. So the subject can actually end the session early.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired: tool exists, is dispatched, the flag is branched on and ends the rollout.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tool description: 'Declare the task cannot be completed and end the session early.' (tools.py:78-79) — task-completion/efficiency framing, no welfare rationale
